main_body: Japanese-style two-roof townhouse: a tiled roof (rows 1-30), a white plaster band (rows 33-40), a lower eave roof (rows 41-47), and a wooden lattice front with a central dark doorway (rows 48-78)
top_band: Column x=32: a ridge cap of blue-grey tones (rows 1-5, L 158/130/83) that is only a 1-5 row stripe. Below it the roof slope (rows 6-30) is drawn face-on as vertical tile stripes in dark tones (L 46-130), with no lighter horizontal top surface.
evidence: The whole piece is stacked flat bands seen straight on: roof tile stripes, plaster wall, lower roof, lattice wall. The ridge is a thin cap line at the top, and the roof slopes are vertical tile columns with no lighter top plane. The plaster band and eave are each a single flat face. The lattice and door are painted flat on the wall with a hint of dark inner edge, not a clearly inset opening. No horizontal surface is visible from above and there is no front-edge line, so it reads as an architectural front elevation, like the red 'front elevation' guide shape.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have about 5 steps and some per-tile highlights, but the candidate is far below both references on the measured facts: 8 colours per tile vs 18 and 11, and 34 distinct colours vs 185 and 66. 72% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline reads as a near-black sticker line. The plaster band and lattice are simple, with little speckle or grain. The references carry richer tile scallops, speckle and tinted outlines, so this piece looks thinner and flatter next to them.
